title: Objection that nothing is future before God's decree: absolute futurity needs a decree, conditional futurity only a supposed one
source_text: XLVIII. Quod si quis dicat nihil futurum esse, nisi dependenter a Dei decreto; & sic ante decretum Dei, rem non esse magis futuram quam non futuram, sed indifferentem ad hoc, ut futura vel non futura sit; adeoque neutrum de ea vere affirmari posse: Respondeo ad hoc, ut res absolute futura sit, praerequiri quidem quoddam Dei decretum, a quo pendeat ejus futuritio: sed ad hoc ut res non sit simpliciter futura, sed tantum futura esset sub aliqua conditione, non requiri decretum quod actu in Deo sit; sed sufficere decretum quod, juxta hypothesin, in Deo ponendum esset.
pass_a_gloss: XLVIII. But if anyone say that nothing is future, except dependently on the decree of God; and so before the decree of God, the thing is not more future than not future, but indifferent to this, that it be future or not future; and so that neither can be truly affirmed of it: I answer that in order that a thing be absolutely future, there is indeed prerequired some decree of God, on which its futurition depends: but in order that a thing be not simply future, but only would be future under some condition, there is not required a decree which is actually in God; but a decree suffices which, according to the hypothesis, would have to be posited in God.
pass_b_english: Someone may object that nothing is future except in dependence on God's decree. Before God's decree, then, a thing is no more future than not future, but open to being either, so that neither can truly be said of it.

My answer is this. For a thing to be absolutely future, some decree of God on which its futurity depends is indeed required beforehand. But for a thing not to be simply future, only future under some condition, no decree actually present in God is needed. It is enough that there be a decree that would have to be posited in God on that hypothesis.

lemmas.gloss: except dependently on the decree of God
there is indeed prerequired some decree of God

choices.why: God's decree; 'decree' is kept throughout, with 'decreed' for decrevit.
